# Held-out check on 30 restaurants (pre-registered)

<!-- heldout30:start (generated by scripts/benchmark-holdout.ts --eval30) -->
The list of 22 new restaurants, the metrics and the decision rule were committed (9a147de) before any model call: [PREREGISTRATION_30.md](PREREGISTRATION_30.md). The run uses the protocol of the 8-restaurant held-out check in [SUMMARY.md](SUMMARY.md) unchanged. Each restaurant's two Qloo sets (the ~150 restaurants its audience loves most and the city's ~150 most popular) are split in half by a seeded hash of the Qloo entity id. The held-out arm sees the crowd-vs-city contrast of half A only, and every arm's three dishes are scored on half B only, with the crowd-lift formula the app shows (src/lib/lift.ts). There are 5 splits (seeds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) with one fresh sample per arm per split. Every arm is the same model (`claude-opus-5-5`) at the same low effort with the app's own no-Qloo prompt; the arms differ only in the Qloo data appended to it.

Run on 2026-10-25 with `npm run eval:heldout`: 600 model calls, 1038999 input and 191766 output tokens, about US$7.99 at list prices. 30 of 30 restaurants completed.

### Result

**Decision on the new restaurants, by the pre-registered rule: not shown: the 95% interval includes ×1, so this sample cannot tell the gain from no difference.** On the 22 new restaurants the held-out arm's dishes score ×1.22 on half B against ×1.11 for the same model with no Qloo data: per restaurant, ×1.10 (95% interval ×0.96 to ×1.27). It beats the model alone in 13 of 22 new restaurants (exact two-sided sign test, p = 0.523) and in 60 of 110 plans.

Headline, by the pre-registered rule (the lower of the new-restaurant and all-restaurant ratios): the 22 new restaurants, ×1.10 (95% interval ×0.96 to ×1.27), better in 13 of 22.

### Limits

- Crowd lift is a proxy: it says the crowd's favourite restaurants serve dishes like these more often than the city's most popular ones, with Qloo's own menu tags as the ruler. It does not measure demand, covers or whether guests would order the dish.
- Half-size sets make each term count noisier, and there is one sample per arm per split.
- The intervals are over these restaurants. They say nothing about cities or kinds of restaurant this list does not cover.
- Both halves come from the same city and the same Qloo audience signal, so this tests whether the contrast carries over to other restaurants this crowd loves.
<!-- heldout30:end -->

## What this run says, in plain words

On 22 restaurants that played no part in building Tastecraft, Qloo's crowd-vs-city contrast moved the model's dishes 10% further towards what each crowd's other favourite places serve (95% interval −4% to +27%), better in 13 of 22. By the rule I committed before the run, that is **not shown**: this sample cannot tell it from no difference. The +27% I published from the first 8 restaurants does not hold up at this size. Run again with fresh samples, those same 8 give +23% (−4% to +63%), and all 30 together give +13% (+0% to +29%).

Two results are clear. First, Qloo's affinity data on its own (the audience's dish and cuisine tags and loved places) made the dishes worse than the model alone on the new restaurants, ×0.85 (×0.73 to ×0.99). Second, the crowd-vs-city contrast fixes that: against affinity data alone it scores ×1.29 (×1.16 to ×1.44) and wins in 19 of 22 new restaurants. Raw affinity leans towards what is popular everywhere; the contrast is what makes Qloo's signal specific to a crowd.

## Where it fails

The held-out arm did not beat the model alone in 12 of the 30 restaurants (9 of the 22 new ones). In 10 of the 12 the model alone already scored above ×1 by staying with the restaurant's own cuisine, and the contrast pulled it towards dishes that the scoring half's crowd places serve no more often than the city's. Part of that is regression to the mean: a high score for the model alone is partly luck, which makes the ratio lower. It loses most at casual places: at $ and $$ it beats the model alone in 3 of 11 new restaurants, at $$$ and $$$$ in 10 of 11 (an exploratory split, not a test). It helps most where the model alone is weak, for example Commander's Palace (×0.72 alone, ×1.59 with the contrast) and Casa Lucio (×0.59, ×1.56).

One line each, from the worst ratio:

- Mustafa's Gemüse Kebap, Berlin (×0.61): alone, the stand's Turkish staples (lahmacun, lentil soup, halloumi dürüm) scored ×1.98; with the contrast it added cheese fries and pistachio cheesecake and scored ×1.21.
- Buddy's Pizza, Detroit (×0.70): alone, Detroit-style squares with Michigan toppings (×1.01); with the contrast, bar food around the pizza such as truffle fries, curry wings and a Reuben square (×0.70).
- Mary Mac's Tea Room, Atlanta (×0.71, lost all 5 splits): alone, family-size Southern classics like fried chicken, chicken and dumplings and cobbler (×1.06); with the contrast, catfish po'boys, wings and egg rolls (×0.75).
- Au Cheval, Chicago, one of the original 8 (×0.73, lost all 5 splits): alone, the diner's own burger kits and fried bologna sandwiches (×1.29); with the contrast, steak frites, skillets and tiramisu jars (×0.95).
- Contramar, Mexico City (×0.75): alone, Mexican seafood such as aguachile, pescado zarandeado and crab tostadas, the second-highest score of the model alone in the run (×1.82); the contrast moved it to paella, arroz negro and risotto (×1.37).
- Bouillon Chartier, Paris (×0.76): alone, the bouillon's own French classics such as boeuf bourguignon and hachis parmentier (×1.59); with the contrast, lasagne and tiramisu (×1.20).
- Lotus of Siam, Las Vegas (×0.84, lost all 5 splits): alone, Northern Thai dishes such as khao soi, gaeng hung lay and mango sticky rice (×1.74); with the contrast, fusion items such as pork belly bao, karaage and jackfruit larb (×1.47).
- The Original Ninfa's on Navigation, Houston (×0.84): alone, fajita packs and birria tacos (×1.06); with the contrast, albóndigas soup, tortas and margarita kits (×0.89).
- Dishoom, London, one of the original 8 (×0.85): alone, Bombay street food (×1.10), although only 8 of its 15 dishes matched a local menu; with the contrast, brunch fusion such as chai tiramisu and fried chicken with waffles (×0.93).
- Versailles Restaurant, Miami (×0.90): alone, Cuban comfort food such as croquetas, ropa vieja and guava pastelitos (×1.03); with the contrast it drifted to Peruvian and seafood plates such as lomo saltado and ceviche (×0.93).
- Mama's Fish House, Maui, one of the original 8 (×0.93): both arms proposed much the same poke and fish tacos and both scored under ×1 (×0.95 and ×0.88); the gap is within noise.
- Hodad's, San Diego (×0.95): both under ×1 (×0.90 alone with burger boxes, ×0.85 with the contrast with breakfast sandwiches and wings); the gap is within noise.

What I would test next, on this same list and with a new pre-registration: keep the restaurant's own cuisine as a constraint when the agent reads the contrast, so the contrast picks among dishes that fit the house instead of replacing them.
